clue.text: Relatively crude one's put away in drawer

indicators.note: one thing put away inside another, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, a sketcher
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone's rather rough possession has been stowed in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but is a person who draws. 'Relatively crude' is a comparative: more rough and unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sketchier is rougher and less finished, comparatively crude.

clue.text: List of clues he'd cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has solved a set of crossword hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' reads as solved, but it is the anagram signal working on CLUES and HED.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or itemised list.

clue.text: Brother runs away from violent quarrel

indicators.note: violent suggests wild disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taken away from the word quarrel, so those letters are removed

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, so two Rs

explanation.surface: A sibling storms out of a fierce family row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes RR (runs) from QUARREL, leaving QUAEL, which 'violent' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother can mean a peer or fellow, one of the same standing.

clue.text: Place that used to be known as 3 and 19, literally

annotationWithheld.why: Place that used to be known as 3 and 19, literally (14): the cross-references 3 and 19 point at entries in the original grid numbering, which this file does not hold (19 here is EXCERPT), so the wordplay cannot be shown.
annotationWithheld.clue: Place that used to be known as 3 and 19, literally

clue.text: Cause fuming in more ways than one

definitions.text: Cause fuming in more ways than one

parts.words: Cause fuming in more ways than one
parts.note: to make someone fume with rage, and also the scented stuff that gives off fumes when burnt

explanation.surface: Something makes people seethe with anger and smoke at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to enrage; incense is also the aromatic substance burnt to give scented smoke.

clue.text: Register put on head's desk

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a roll is an official register of names
the head or top of something

explanation.surface: A school register has been left on the headteacher's desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the headteacher but simply means top.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-top is a desk with a sliding slatted cover.

clue.text: Wander idly in southern Nigeria

parts.note: WAN is the international vehicle code for Nigeria

explanation.surface: Someone drifts about aimlessly in the south of Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: WAN is Nigeria's international vehicle registration code.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan around is idiomatic for moving about idly or aimlessly.

clue.text: Silver bearer?

parts.note: not a carrier of cutlery but something that supported Long John Silver, the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island

explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver in Treasure Island stood on a peg leg of timber.

clue.text: One gets out of the habit

definitions.text: One gets out of the habit

parts.words: One gets out of the habit
parts.note: habit is clothing, as a nun's habit, so this is someone who takes off all clothes

explanation.definitionFit: A naturist strips off all clothing, getting out of any garment at all.

clue.text: Crushed cheeky old bottom in spanking

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, cutting it open

parts.note: spanking and bumper both mean very large or excellent, as a bumper crop
pert means saucy or cheeky
bum is British slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A saucy old backside got crushed during a smacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanking' looks like a punishment but is the adjective meaning very big or excellent; the cheeky old bottom goes inside it, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic that is bumper-to-bumper is jammed tightly together, crushed nose to tail.

clue.text: For example, twins throw up spew alternately

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Twin children are being sick, one after the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twins' is Gemini, one of the twelve astrological houses or signs.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac called houses.

clue.text: Slippery crude oil lines run away into film

indicators.note: slippery suggests things sliding around, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for run goes away from the word crude

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
L is an abbreviation for line, so two Ls

explanation.surface: Oily pipelines leak into a film production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R (run) from CRUDE; CUDE, OIL and LL are then rearranged by 'Slippery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celluloid was the plastic base of cinema film, so it stands for movies.

clue.text: Swimmer in row outside old London public house originally

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, surrounding it

parts.note: a din is a loud row or racket

indicators.note: taking the original, that is first, letter of each word

explanation.surface: A swimmer is caught up in a fight outside a historic London pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is the noise sense, DIN, not a line or a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal that swims.

clue.text: Stop and bless when this is this

indicators.note: when each word loses its top, that is its first letter, the leading letters are removed

explanation.surface: A riddle about two words when they are in a certain state.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-referential: STOP and BLESS, each without its top letter (S and B), become TOP and LESS, which together spell the state they are in.
explanation.definitionFit: The final 'this' stands for the state being described, missing the top.

clue.text: Minute postal order left out as peers lay?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A postal order has been briefly misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' is the adjective meaning not of the clergy, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The secular members of the House of Lords, as opposed to the bishops, are lay peers.

clue.text: Opera success by Latvian in foreign resort

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the resort name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a resort abroad
a go can mean a success, as in make a go of it
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: An opera triumphs thanks to a Baltic singer at a holiday spot abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's work about a jester is a celebrated opera.

clue.text: Green Party are mostly off playing some music

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with, rearranged
letters taken off, removed from the fodder
mostly means losing the last letter of the word are

explanation.surface: The Greens are largely out playing a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ARE to AR; 'off' removes AR from GREENPARTY, and 'playing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieg wrote incidental music for Ibsen's play of that name.

clue.text: Girls smacked by him cried, we were once told

definitions.text: Girls smacked by him cried, we were once told

parts.words: Girls smacked by him cried, we were once told
parts.note: smacked is kissed, from a smacker; in the childhood nursery rhyme a boy kissed the girls and made them cry

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme character kissed the girls and made them weep.

clue.text: Table in general is to have a bright sheen

indicators.note: one piece is inside the other

parts.note: a list is a table of items

explanation.surface: A table is bound to shine in general.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with a wet sparkle.

clue.text: Exclude without right extract

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the word goes around the letter

parts.note: to except is to exclude

explanation.surface: Leaving out the correct passage of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer work.

clue.text: Film about Young Conservative, frightfully posh

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the other piece
frightfully suggests things in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: YC is the abbreviation for a Young Conservative

explanation.surface: A film about a terribly upper-class young Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightfully' looks like an intensifier of 'posh' in the surface, but it is the anagram signal; 'about' puts the rearranged letters around the Young Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's horror classic is a famous movie.

clue.text: Programmes "Bill", say, in retransmission

indicators.note: sent out again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A programme called Bill is being repeated on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programmes' looks like broadcasts, but means courses of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabi are outlines of study, programmes for a course.

clue.text: One at the eighteenth tee or the nineteenth hole?

definitions.text: One at the eighteenth tee or the nineteenth hole?

parts.words: One at the eighteenth tee or the nineteenth hole?
parts.note: a golfer wields a club on the tee; the nineteenth hole is the clubhouse bar, so a frequenter of a nightclub

explanation.definitionFit: A club-goer frequents nightclubs, and a golfer swings a club.

clue.text: Prohibition on following female in northern town

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the following ones

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A ban on women is in force in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: BANFF is a town in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a coastal town in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Sanitary arrangement for kittens?

parts.note: kittens being young cats, their toilet provision is the granules put in a tray

explanation.definitionFit: Cats use a tray of absorbent granules as their toilet.

clue.text: Bloomer put bridge partnership in the money

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pay is the money earned
North and South are a partnership at bridge, NS

explanation.surface: A bridge pair are put in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake or loaf, but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A pansy is a garden flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: Sort of gong covering old instrument

indicators.note: one piece covers, that is goes around, the other

parts.note: an OBE is an honour, slang gong

explanation.surface: A kind of gong is draped over an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour, here the OBE, not a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: What's clear, if portent's interpreted

indicators.note: interpreted means read another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word portent, with 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: An omen is explained to show what is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' is the verb sense: to earn after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: What you clear is the earnings left after all costs, the bottom-line gain.
